title: Badshah Just Signed a Global Deal with Universal Music Group. Capitol Records and EMI Will Release His Music Worldwide.
excerpt: The Delhi-born rapper becomes the first Indian artist to secure a multi-year exclusive partnership with UMG spanning recordings, publishing, and brand licensing across 180 markets.
body:
Universal Music Group has announced an exclusive global agreement with Badshah, the Delhi-born rapper, singer, and music producer who has generated more than 15 billion streams worldwide. The multi-year deal covers future recordings, music publishing rights for non-film compositions, and brand licensing and partnerships across UMG's network of 60-plus territories covering 180 markets.

The partnership will be led by Universal Music India, with global priority support from Capitol Records in the United States and EMI in the United Kingdom. The first tracks under the new arrangement are expected later this summer, and UMG says the plan is to pair Badshah with influential artists from around the world.

## What the Deal Means

This is not a distribution arrangement or a one-off licensing agreement. It is a permanent, full-spectrum partnership that positions Badshah as UMG's flagship Indian artist for the global market. Sir Lucian Grainge, UMG's chairman and CEO, described it in terms that the label typically reserves for its highest-priority signings: "We are delighted to partner with Badshah, one of India's most respected and popular artists, for the next phase of his career, as we put the weight of our global company behind him to introduce his music to new audiences worldwide."

Devraj Sanyal, the MD and CEO of Universal Music India and South Asia, went further. He called the signing one of those defining moments in music history for a region, comparing the potential trajectory to what K-pop and reggaeton achieved in the last decade. "The greatest popstar that India has ever produced now moves his permanent house to join us at UMG," Sanyal said. "I'm confident that India's time has come."

## The Numbers Behind the Name

Badshah is the only Indian artist in history to have achieved 15 songs with more than 200 million video views each on YouTube. The list includes Paani Paani, Genda Phool, She Move It Like, Paagal, Kala Chashma, DJ Waley Babu, Garmi, and Mercy. He has performed more than 700 live shows and built a brand ambassadorship portfolio that spans global consumer names.

His career is now in its twentieth year. He started as Aditya Prateek Singh Sisodia from a middle-class Punjabi family in Delhi, broke through with Saturday Saturday in 2012, and built a sound that fuses Punjabi folk elements with contemporary hip-hop beats. His third studio album Ek Tha Raja, released in collaboration with Karan Aujla, DIVINE, and Raftaar, confirmed his position at the centre of India's independent music ecosystem.

## Why This Matters for the Diaspora

For NRI audiences who have been streaming Badshah's music at weddings, Diwali parties, and road trips for a decade, this deal formalises what they already knew: Indian pop music has a global audience. The UMG infrastructure — Capitol Records in the US, EMI in the UK, local labels in 60-plus territories — means Badshah's future releases will receive the same marketing, playlist placement, and radio promotion pipeline that UMG provides to its Western pop roster.

Adam Granite, UMG's EVP of market development, drew the comparison explicitly. "Like reggaeton and K-pop in recent years," he said, Indian music "has the opportunity to inspire new generations of music fans everywhere." The framing is deliberate: it positions Indian music not as a niche curiosity but as the next global genre.

Badshah put it more simply. "I want to make music for everybody and bring the vibrance of India to the world with my music," he said. "I am someone purely driven by the power of dreams and the game plan with the teams at Universal Music is to bring all of them to life."

The first tracks from the partnership are expected this summer.
